title: רב אחא בר יעקב

paragraphs: Rav Acha bar Yaakov. His academy was at Pappunya, Kiddushin 35a; Bava Kamma 54b; he instituted a practice there, Niddah 67b. Of sixty elders at Rav Huna’s lectures, all but him became sterile from delaying urination, fulfilling “Wisdom preserves its possessor” (see there). When livelihood occupied him, he borrowed study time by day and repaid at night, chapter Haddar 65a. Rava praised him to Rav Nachman as a great man, Bava Kamma 40a; Yoma 46a: Rava said, “Who is this who does not care for his flour?” He excelled in wisdom and age (see Rabbi Elazar of Hagrunya). He expounded that Satan and Peninnah intended Heaven’s sake, and Satan came and kissed his feet, Bava Batra 16a. Sukkah 38a: waving the lulav, he said, “An arrow in Satan’s eyes!” Why did Satan not distress him as Pelimo, who regularly said this? Perhaps he said it only with the lulav, not daily; or Satan kissed him because he expounded in his defense. He wrote a Torah scroll [מ״ת; exact expansion unresolved] on calfskins, its length equaling its circumference. The sages cast their eyes on him and he died, Bava Batra 14a. He was accustomed to miracles, killing the seven-headed harmful being in Abaye’s academy (as the concubine’s husband’s reincarnation; see Abaye at length). Megalleh Amukkot, no.192: the seven heads were Esau’s seven impure powers. Samael, Esau’s prince, has seven names, is the Angel of Death and evil inclination. Jacob bowed seven times against these heads, subduing them through his Shema. Esau’s “I have much, my brother” hints at Rav Acha; hence bar Yaakov: Jacob gave him the power to fell the seven heads. “He wished to do this” [וזה רצה עשה לעשות; wording irregular]. אעברה נ״א gives the initials “serpent, Acha” [נחש אחא]; see there. Tosafot, Shabbat 139, end of a, on giving to an Israelite child, have a tradition that the questioner was Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov. Likewise Tosafot, Eruvin 40b: “The law does not follow Rav Acha bar Yaakov.” Rashi: where this occurred is not specified; Tosafot: they have a tradition, etc. Rabbi Acha bar Tachlifa; Rav Acha bar Ika, his sister’s son; Rabbi Elazar of Hagrunya were punished because of him (see there). Rabbi Abba bar Zavda, his colleague; Abaye (see above). Rabbi Ilai said in Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov’s name, in our master’s name (Rashi: Rav), Berakhot 22a. Apparently this led She'erit Yosef to count him among Rav’s students. But he was Rav Huna’s student, as above, and Rav Huna was Rav’s student; this requires examination. Rav Giddel, his colleague; Rav Huna, his teacher (see above). In Rabbi Zeira’s name, Yoma 55a. He challenged Rachava’s report in Rabbi Yehudah’s name. He spoke to Rabbi Chiyya of Hormiz-Ardashir in Rav Nachman bar Yaakov’s name, Chezkat Habattim 52a. Concerning Rabbi Chama he said, “The world is handed to fools” (see there), but Ein Yaakov has Rav Chisda, and the Gemara has Rav Acha; requires examination. In Rabbi Yochanan’s name, Hammaddir 74a. In Rav Nachman’s time (see there). Rav Pappa sat before him, Chullin 33a. Rava praised him and said he did not care for flour (see above). Rav Sheshet, his colleague; Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, his father; Rabbi Yaakov, his brother; Rabbi Yaakov, his daughter’s son.
